This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 16.03.2020 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-VII, at Vijayapura, in MVC No.2029/2014.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 28.09.2014 at about 07.15 p.m., when the deceased Shrimant S/o Ramu Gaganmali was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/H-7631 from Tikota to Bijapur, at that time, a Tractor and two Trailers were wrongly parked in the middle of the road.

There were no indicators to the last NC:
2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR trailer bearing registration No.MH-10/W-8170 and even no fencing of stones or no light was set in to indicate the parked vehicle.
The deceased dashed his motorcycle to the said trailer, as a result of which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. On service of summons, respondent Nos.2 and 3 appeared through counsel and filed their written statements denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal and hence, was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.3 as PW-1 and another witness as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.

sentences.text: The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent act of both the driver of the Tractor and trailer and the rider of the motorcycle.
As a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.13,60,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay only to the extent of 50% of the entire compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Learned counsel appearing for the claimants has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.MH-10/W-8170 attached to the tractor.
The accident occurred at about 07.15 p.m.
The tractor and NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR two trailers were wrongly parked in the middle of the road.
There were no indicators to the last trailer bearing registration No.MH-10-W/8170.
Since it was dark, the deceased-rider of the motorcycle was unable to see the parked trailer in the middle of the road.
Due to negligence of parking trailer in the middle of the road, the accident has occurred and Srimanth died.
He further contended that Tribunal has wrongly held that deceased has contributed to the accident only on the ground that he was not holding driving licence.
There is no material to prove that deceased has contributed to the accident.
In support of his contention, he relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sudhir Kumar Rana vs. Surinder Singh And Others [(2008) 12 SCC 436].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he has contended that the finding of the Tribunal that deceased has contributed 50% to the accident is unsustainable.
b) In respect of quantum, he has contended that at the time of the accident, deceased was aged about 45 NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR years.
He was earning of Rs.25,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has assessed notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month which is on the lower side.

c) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi And Others [AIR 2017 SC 5157], in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 25% of the established income towards 'future prospects' should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 50 years.

Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants are entitled for Ramu S/O Laxman Ganganmali And Ors vs Suresh S/O Babaso Patil And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114883392/

7. Per contra, Sri Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the deceased as well as the driver of the tractor.
The claimants have not impleaded the driver and insurer of the tractor as a party.
The second respondent insurer is insured with only second trailer bearing registration No.MH-10/W-8170.
Therefore, he contended that owner of the tractor as well as the insurer of the tractor have to be made liable for negligence.
a) He further contended that the Tribunal failed to consider that the driver of the tractor is negligent in causing the accident.

Even if it is held that it is a NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR composite negligence, liberty may be reserved to the insurer of the trailer bearing registration No.MH-10/W- 8170 to initiate separate proceedings against the driver of the tractor and insurer.

In support of his contention, he has relied on judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Khenyei vs. New India Assurance Company Lomitted And Others [(2015) 9 SCC 273].
b) In respect of quantum of compensation he contended that even though claimants have claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, they have not produced any document to establish the same.

c) Lastly, he contended that considering the material available on record, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and therefore, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

9. The case of the claimants is that on 28.09.2014 at about 07.15 p.m., the deceased was driving a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/H-7631 towards Bijapur from Tikota side, at that time, a tractor and two trailers were wrongly parked in the middle of the road.
There were no indicators to the last trailer bearing registration No.MH-10/W-8170.
Since it was evening, the parking of the tractor and trailer was not visible and there were no stone fencing and no indicators indicating the parking of the vehicle.
The rider of the motorcycle hit the last trailer.
Due to the impact, he suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal on appreciation of documentary and oral evidence of the parties has given a clear finding that the accident has occurred due to negligence of the trailer bearing registration No.MH-10/W- 8170.

Since trailer was wrongly parked in the middle Ramu S/O Laxman Ganganmali And Ors vs Suresh S/O Babaso Patil And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114883392/
5 of the road in the night, there were no indicators to the last - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR trailer and no light set in and there was no stone fencing to indicate the parked vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In spite of giving such a finding only because charge sheet has been filed against the deceased for not holding a driving licence, 50% of the contributory negligence has been fastened on the deceased.

10. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Sudhir Kumar Rana (supra), held that though driving vehicle without licence is an offence, but same by itself may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
The relevant paragraphs are paragraph Nos.8 and 9 and the same are extracted hereunder for easy reference:

"8. In T.O.Anthony Vs.Karvaranan [(2008) 3 SCC 748] it was held that:
"6. 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons.
Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrongdoers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrongdoers.

In such a case, each wrongdoer is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR against all or any of them.

In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrongdoer separately,
nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrongdoer separately.

On the other hand where a person suffers injury, partly due to the negligence on the part of another person or persons, and partly as a result of his own negligence, then the negligence on the part of the injured which contributed to the accident is referred to as his contributory negligence.

Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stand reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence.

7. Therefore, when two vehicles are involved in an accident, and one of the drivers claims compensation from the other driver alleging negligence, and the other driver denies negligence or claims that the injured claimant himself was negligent, then it becomes necessary to consider whether the injured claimant was negligent and if so,
whether he was solely or partly responsible for the accident and the extent of his responsibility, that is, his contributory negligence.

Therefore where the injured is himself partly liable, the principle of 'composite negligence' will not apply nor can there be an automatic inference that the negligence was 50:50 as has been assumed Ramu S/O Laxman Ganganmali And Ors vs Suresh S/O Babaso Patil And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114883392/
6 in this case.

entities.text: Laxman Ganganmali And Ors vs Suresh S/O Babaso Patil And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal ought to have examined the extent of contributory negligence of the appellant and thereby avoided confusion between composite negligence and contributory - 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR negligence.
The High Court has failed to correct the said error."
9. If a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.
The same, by itself, in our opinion, may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini truck who was driving rashly and negligently.
It is one thing to say that the appellant was not possessing any licence but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two-wheeler rashly and negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having a licence, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence."

11. Even the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Mohammed Siddiqui vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others, [(2020) 3 SCC 57], held that the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.

entities.text: Mohammed Siddiqui vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others, [(2020) 3 SCC 57]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence unless it is established - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
12. There is no finding by the Tribunal to prove that the deceased has contributed to the accident.
Therefore, finding of the Tribunal to the extent that deceased has contributed 50% to the accident is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, it is set aside.
13. Though the claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, they have not produced any document to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident taken place in the year 2014, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.10,000/- p.m.

To the aforesaid income, 25% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'Pranay Sethi'
- 15 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.12,500/-.

Since there are six dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased Ramu S/O Laxman Ganganmali And Ors vs Suresh S/O Babaso Patil And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114883392/
7 towards personal expenses and remaining amount has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '14'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs,15,75,000/- (Rs.9,375*12*14)
on account of 'loss of dependency'.
14. In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

15. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'Magma General Insurance'
(supra), claimant Nos.1 and 2, are parents of the deceased are entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of filial consortium', claimant No.3, wife of the deceased is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/-
- 16 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4533-DB HC-KAR under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium' and claimant Nos.4 to 6 children of the deceased are entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium'.

16. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)

 (12500 x  x 12 x 14)
Funeral expenses 15,000/-

Loss of estate 15,000/-

17.

ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
